# University ontology: lens scaling results

**Date:** 2026-09-26 to 2026-09-28
**Model:** google/gemma-4-E4B-it (42 layers, hidden size 2560), bf16, one RTX 3090
**Ontology:** university builder skeleton (`results/ontology_skeleton_v2.json`, generated by gemma-3-4b-it) with context-aware MELDs
**Stage:** training pass only. No sibling refinement or calibration on the v3 packs.

## Question

How does held-out lens quality scale with the training data, and which kind of data is worth generating? Four axes:

1. **Samples per concept** at a fixed budget (HatCat's templated generator).
2. **Definition depth:** how many levels of definition-only descendants feed each lens (0, Schools, Schools + Departments).
3. **Lateral links:** cross-branch "related" links, shared topics and diagonal negatives derived from embedding similarity.
4. **"Differs because" contrasts:** generated boundary examples for every pair of concepts a lens must separate.

## Setup

- **Lenses.** Band probes: one MLP probe per model-layer band (early, mid, late), chosen per concept by `select_layers_for_concept`, saved as `Concept@L<n>.pt` and combined by mean. The grid uses 26 University lenses (2 per Field) with band layers fixed across every configuration, so only the data varies.
- **Held-out text.** The builder holds out 30% of Departments (skeleton level 4) by a hash of their tree path (`--holdout-level 4`), so the split is identical in every pack. The test text is their cleaned topic descriptions: 20 per University, 3,260 in total, none seen in training at any depth.
- **Metrics.**
  - Per-lens AUROC: a lens's own held-out texts against everyone else's (**all**), or against only its siblings' and cross-linked concepts' (**hard**, the disambiguation that matters). Rank-based, so no calibration is involved.
  - Whole packs are also ranked lens against lens (top-1, top-3, median rank). That mixes discrimination with how hot each lens runs, so it is harsher before calibration.
- **Chance:** AUROC 0.5; top-1 0.6% and median rank 83 of 165.

## Results

### Fixed templated budget (hard / all AUROC, mean of bands)

| Pack | 20 | 40 | 80 | 160 |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Depth 0 | 0.665 / 0.692 | 0.666 / 0.692 | 0.658 / 0.698 | 0.637 / 0.681 |
| Depth 1 | 0.666 / 0.685 | 0.702 / 0.722 | 0.711 / 0.749 | 0.709 / 0.757 |
| Depth 1, links | 0.662 / 0.682 | 0.698 / 0.734 | 0.714 / 0.748 | 0.700 / 0.743 |
| Depth 2 | 0.655 / 0.661 | 0.704 / 0.721 | 0.708 / 0.738 | 0.706 / 0.743 |
| Depth 2, child links | 0.636 / 0.660 | 0.666 / 0.706 | 0.658 / 0.705 | 0.673 / 0.720 |

### Content budget (real text only)

| Pack | Positives per lens | AUROC all | AUROC hard | Early / mid / late (hard) | Minutes |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Depth 1 | ~22 | 0.795 | 0.714 | 0.738 / 0.619 / 0.682 | 3 |
| Depth 1 + contrasts | ~85 | 0.839 | 0.799 | 0.801 / 0.705 / 0.776 | 12 |
| Depth 2 | ~106 | 0.890 | 0.784 | 0.794 / 0.716 / 0.770 | 15 |
| Depth 2 + contrasts | ~168 | 0.899 | 0.820 | 0.826 / 0.746 / 0.797 | 23 |

### Whole packs (165 University lenses, mean of bands)

| Pack | Top-1 | Top-3 | Median rank | AUROC all | AUROC hard | Fields top-1 | Fields median |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| v1: templated, refined | 4.7% | 10.7% | 46 | 0.653 | 0.634 | 19.1% | 5 |
| v2: depth 1 + links, refined | 6.7% | 14.5% | 30 | 0.734 | 0.697 | 22.8% | 4 |
| v3: depth 2, content budget | 10.6% | 27.5% | 9 | 0.889 | 0.789 | 32.6% | 3 |
| v3 + contrasts | 16.9% | 33.7% | 7 | 0.896 | 0.822 | 34.1% | 2 |

The 26-lens grid predicted the full pack: 0.820 hard AUROC in the grid, 0.822 across all 165 lenses.

## Findings

1. **More templated samples don't help.** At depth 0, going from 20 to 160 samples costs 8× the training time and loses 0.028 hard AUROC: past the ~10 MELD examples, extra samples are rewordings of the same sentences. This matches HatCat's earlier knee at 10–40 samples (`PHASE_HISTORY.md`, Phase 1).
2. **Samples pay off only with new content behind them.** Under the fixed budget, depth 1 (Schools' definitions as a quarter of positives) beats depth 0 by +0.045 hard, and keeps improving to 80 samples.
3. **A content-only budget beats every templated budget.** Training on real text only (MELD examples + descendant definitions, no templates) matches the best templated hard AUROC at depth 1 with ~22 positives, a quarter of the samples, and beats it against all negatives (0.795 vs 0.757).
4. **Deeper descendants pay off once they are the budget.** Under the fixed budget, depth 2 showed no gain over depth 1 (it could fill only a quarter of positives). With the content budget, depth 2 (~106 positives) reaches 0.784 hard and 0.890 all: the fractal inheritance works when the sample count scales with the content.
5. **"Differs because" contrasts do the disambiguation.** They add +0.085 hard at depth 1 and +0.036 at depth 2, and are the best configuration overall (0.820 hard / 0.899 all). Across the whole pack they raise University top-1 from 10.6% to 16.9%.
6. **Embedding-derived negatives don't substitute for contrasts.**
   - Cross-links and diagonal negatives made no difference at depth 1.
   - Derived from Department overlaps, they hurt at depth 2 under a fixed budget (0.708 → 0.673 best), by flooding each lens with ~240 near-topic hard negatives.
   - That curve was the only one still rising at 160 samples, so those hard negatives may need a budget that grows with them.
   - The content budget doesn't use diagonal negatives yet (see open questions).
7. **Band pattern.** In every configuration the early band is strongest and the mid band weakest. More content lifts all three; the mid band gains most (0.62 → 0.75 hard).

## Per-probe calibration and the band combiner (2026-10-01)

Band probes are independent readings of one concept from different depths, so a lens should fire when any one of them stands out. Raw probe scores aren't comparable across layers, though. So each probe is calibrated on its own background, as the fraction of background it exceeds (`scripts/calibrate_band_probes.py`), and the lens takes the **max of calibrated probes**.

Cross-lens ranking on the test half of the held-out split (1,630 texts; the even half is the calibration background):

| Universities | Raw mean | Raw max | Calibrated max |
|---|---|---|---|
| v3 + contrasts, top-1 | 17.6% | 16.4% | **18.3%** |
| v3, top-1 | 11.3% | 11.2% | **17.2%** |

- **Per-lens AUROC hardly changes with the combiner** (within ~0.006). The combiner matters for comparing lenses against each other.
- **Z-scoring instead of percentiles is worse,** because heavy-tailed probes dominate the max.
- **For Fields, the calibrated max is within noise of the raw mean.**
- **Uncalibrated fallback:** HAT now takes the max of calibrated probes when a pack has `probe_calibration.json`, and the mean of raw probes otherwise.

**Calibrate in the unit the runtime reads.** HAT scores single-token hidden states during generation. Calibration on mean-pooled descriptions saturated at runtime: nearly every top detection read 1.00. Recalibrating on per-token states sampled from the same background texts (`--unit tokens`, now the default, ~13k states) brought top-10 detections at ≥ 0.999 down to 4–10%.

**HAT demo** (Gemma 4 E4B-it, v3 + contrasts, 40 generated tokens per prompt, ~22 of 178 lenses resident, ~30 ms per token):
- **Rail-yard housing question:** UrbanPlanning, UrbanPlanningInfrastructureSystems, UrbanEconomicsRegionalDevelopment.
- **Grief message:** DeathRitualsAndGriefStudies on every token, alongside TraumaInformedStudies, FamilyDynamics and Resilience.
- **Supply-chain sabotage request:**
  - while the model refuses, the readings are InternationalSecurityStudies, PoliticalViolenceResearch and CyberConflictAndInformationWarfare;
  - as it pivots to resilience, they shift to StrategicRiskAnalysisForecasting and GlobalSupplyChainOptimization.

  The same topic reads differently depending on stance.
- **Single-layer senses:** on `' argument'`, the Dialogue lens reads L1 0.09, L14 0.48, L40 0.97. Only the late layer carries that sense, which a mean would dilute.

## Similarity-picked negatives and content refinement (2026-10-01)

**Diagonal negatives under the content budget.** These are depth 2 with child links, content + contrasts runs, 26 lenses, with negatives drawn from a concept's embedding-similar neighbours in other branches (`--diagonal-cap`):

| Negatives | AUROC all | AUROC hard |
|---|---|---|
| Real text from other concepts (cap 0) | 0.892 | 0.815 |
| 100 diagonal texts replace most of that | 0.798 | 0.781 |
| 200 diagonal texts, no other fill | 0.788 | 0.775 |
| 100 diagonal texts on top of the full fill | 0.850 | 0.790 |

The more a lens's negatives come from similarity-picked neighbours, the worse it gets. Adding them on top of an intact fill still costs 0.025 hard, so the damage isn't only lost breadth. Three reasons:
- **Breadth is lost** when they replace the fill, which removes the general background a lens needs to reject.
- **No stated boundary.** Close-but-unexplained neighbours give the probe a boundary with no stated difference to follow.
- **Arbitrary test labels.** There are 7,194 cross-University Department pairs at ≥ 0.9 similarity, so some held-out text is filed arbitrarily between two Universities, and training against those neighbours rejects text that is effectively the lens's own topic.

Similarity should nominate pairs for "differs because" adjudication (merge, share, or state the difference), never supply negatives directly. Contrasts gave +0.036 to +0.085; raw similarity cost up to −0.04.

**Sibling refinement with content prompts.** Refinement ranks siblings' and cross-linked concepts' probes on prompts about each concept. It now uses the concept's authored text (MELD examples, descendant definitions, boundary positives) instead of templates. The run was v3 + contrasts, 30 prompts per member, ~25 min. Training accuracy on the refinement groups went from 40% to 64% (Fields) and from 36% to 61% (Universities). On the held-out test half:

| Universities | Unrefined | Refined |
|---|---|---|
| Top-1 (calibrated max / mean) | 18.3% / 17.6% | 19.1% / 19.5% |
| Top-3 (calibrated max / mean) | 35.0% / 33.7% | 36.4% / 37.1% |
| AUROC hard (calibrated max / mean) | 0.811 / 0.817 | 0.816 / 0.825 |
| Median rank | 7 | 7 |

The gain is small but holds for every combiner. Unlike templated refinement on v1, which worsened median rank from 43 to 48, it hurts nothing. Fields are unchanged. Keep it as a polish stage; the large effects are content, depth and contrasts.

## Costs (this machine)

| Step | Size | Time |
|---|---|---|
| Build a depth-2 concept pack (embedding, cross-linking) | 19,593 concepts | ~65 s CPU |
| Generate contrasts, batched Gemma 4 E4B-it | 1,121 pairs, 11,210 boundary examples | ~45 min |
| Train v3, content budget | 178 lenses, 534 probes | 1 h 55 min |
| Train v3 + contrasts | 178 lenses, 534 probes | 2 h 57 min |
| Held-out evaluation, whole pack | 3,260 texts | ~1 min |

Depth costs generation, not lenses: training cost follows the number of lenses and the content per lens, not the depth of the descendants.

## Pipeline changes

- `scripts/build_skeleton_concept_pack.py` builds a concept pack from a skeleton and its MELDs:
  - concept names instead of institutions, and topic descriptions from cleaned scopes plus children;
  - definition-only descendants (`--definition-levels`), inherited up the tree;
  - cross-branch links, with child-level evidence normalised and capped per concept (`--no-child-links` to disable);
  - a deterministic held-out split (`--holdout-level`);
  - contrast attachment (`--contrasts`).
- `scripts/generate_contrasts.py` generates "differs because" pairs: a distinction sentence plus boundary examples on both sides.
- `src/map/training/sumo_data_generation.py`:
  - `create_content_dataset` builds the content budget;
  - descendants are never negatives for their own ancestors, and shared topics are excluded;
  - the ancestor lookup is now linear (it was quadratic in pack size, about 2 minutes per pool at 19.6k concepts).
- `src/map/training/sumo_classifiers.py`:
  - `--budget content` is the default; concepts without authored text fall back to the adaptive templated path;
  - content-mode concepts train in one pass, extracting activations once for all bands;
  - `--band-probes` trains independent per-band probes;
  - the layer scan takes one forward pass instead of one per layer.
- `src/map/training/sibling_ranking.py`: band-aware refinement, with related concepts added to groups, inputs normalised as in training, and top-level concepts refined as a group. Prompts come from a concept's authored content when it has some.
- `scripts/calibrate_band_probes.py`: per-probe percentile calibration, per-token by default, written to the lens pack as `probe_calibration.json`.
- `scripts/scaling_experiment.py` and `scripts/eval_lens_confusion.py`: the grid and the whole-pack held-out evaluation.

## Open questions

- **Calibration and refinement.** Everything above except the calibration section is the training pass. HatCat's calibration cycle assumes one model layer per pack and single-file lenses, so it needs band-probe support before it can run on v3. Sibling refinement is band-aware but still uses templated prompts; it should use content.
- **Cross-branch adjudication.** Embedding-similar pairs across branches should go through the contrast generator: merge or share them, or give each pair a "differs because". Feeding them in as negatives directly hurts (see above).
- **Contrast-aware graduation.** Graduate a lens when it separates every contrast's boundary set, instead of a single F1 threshold.
- **Generator.** The skeleton, MELDs and contrasts all come from small local models. The 216 names flagged in `name_review.json`, skeleton duplicates and generic repeated Departments suggest a stronger ontologist would help.
- **Noise.** The grid is 26 lenses and one seed; differences under ~0.01 AUROC are not meaningful.

## Reproduce

```
# concept packs (CPU)
python scripts/build_skeleton_concept_pack.py --skeleton results/ontology_skeleton_v2.json \
  --melds results/context_aware_melds --max-level 2 --definition-levels 2 --no-child-links \
  --holdout-level 4 --pack-id university-v3
python scripts/generate_contrasts.py --concept-pack university-exp-d1 --layer 1 --model google/gemma-4-E4B-it \
  --output results/contrasts/university-exp-d1.jsonl      # and --layer 0 -> university-exp-d1-l0.jsonl
python scripts/build_skeleton_concept_pack.py ... --contrasts results/contrasts/university-exp-d1.jsonl \
  --contrasts results/contrasts/university-exp-d1-l0.jsonl --pack-id university-v3-contrasts

# train (content budget is the default)
python -m src.map.training.train_concept_pack_lenses --concept-pack university-v3-contrasts \
  --model google/gemma-4-E4B-it --output-dir lens_packs/gemma-4-e4b-it_university-v3-contrasts-bands \
  --multi-layer --band-probes --no-sibling-refinement

# evaluate on the held-out split
python scripts/eval_lens_confusion.py --lens-pack lens_packs/gemma-4-e4b-it_university-v3-contrasts-bands \
  --concept-pack university-v3 --skeleton results/ontology_skeleton_v2.json --melds results/context_aware_melds \
  --model google/gemma-4-E4B-it --held-out split --max-per-concept 20
```

Summary data: `2026-09-28_university_lens_scaling.json` (next to this file). Full per-concept results are in the untracked `results/scaling/university_gemma4_*.json` and `results/overnight/eval_*.json`.
